data.narrative:
Thea Energy is a Series B nuclear energy company founded by Brian Berzin that has raised $20M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 peers across the nuclear sector—3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Valar Atomics.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach, using a $100M base valuation anchored to total capital raised and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $190M. Peer-median valuation cannot be applied; while 4 same-sector peers exist in the dataset, none satisfy the screen for same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with sufficient sample size (minimum 3 datapoints required). Relying on all-sector medians would introduce excessive methodological noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $162M (low) to $218M (high), with a median of $190M. This range reflects sensitivity around the stage-progression multiplier and the nascent state of nuclear technology company comparable data. Key uncertainties include limited public benchmarks at Thea's specific stage and capital intensity profile, as well as execution risk inherent in pre-revenue or early-revenue frontier-tech ventures. The single-method triangulation constrains confidence; a Series C round incorporating more normalized peer data would strengthen conviction.
